name: Learning patterns that transfer
gist: Building foundation models and using transfer learning so that knowledge learned on one time series task or dataset generalizes to new ones without retraining from scratch.
explain: A trained model on one dataset often fails on a new dataset. A forecasting model trained on 10 years of New York weather will give bad predictions for Boston. A model trained on one patient's heart rate patterns will not generalize to another patient because bodies are different. This is the transfer learning or generalization problem. Ideally, you could train once on a large, diverse dataset, then quickly adapt that knowledge to new sequences without retraining from scratch. This saves compute because you do not redo the expensive large-scale training, reduces data requirements because you reuse knowledge learned elsewhere, and enables models to be deployed faster because adaptation is quicker than full training.

Why is transfer so hard for sequences? Sequences carry many hidden factors. Weather patterns depend on latitude, time of year, and local geography. Heart rates depend on age, fitness, current stress, and medications. Factory sensor readings depend on equipment model, operating conditions, and maintenance history. A model trained on one distribution often overfits to spurious correlations in that distribution. For example, a weather model might learn that 'when the forecast says rain, the next day is cooler'—but that is because rain and cooler temperatures are correlated in the training location, not a causal rule. When transferred to a new location where the correlation differs, the model fails. Transfer learning requires learning the invariant patterns that actually generalize.

Papers build foundation models—large models trained on many diverse sequences from different domains and sources. The idea is that if a model sees sequences from factories, hospitals, finance, and climate science simultaneously, it learns general principles about how sequences work rather than domain-specific quirks. Then, for a new sequence, you fine-tune just a small part of the model or add a small adapter. Some papers also investigate what features transfer: do models that understand seasonal patterns transfer well, even if the specific seasons differ? Others use domain adversarial training, where you force the model to be unable to tell which domain a sequence came from, so it must learn domain-invariant representations.

papers.title: FeDaL: Federated Dataset Learning for General Time Series Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates cross-dataset generalization improvements across eight tasks with analysis of federated scaling behavior under decentralization.

papers.title: Repurposing Foundation Model for Generalizable Medical Time Series Classification
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 35% absolute F1-score improvement over specialized baselines through lightweight label query training requiring only 0.1% of parameters.

papers.title: Understanding the Implicit Biases of Design Choices for Time Series Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Characterizes how inductive biases in TSFMs affect fundamental properties like temporal behavior and mean reversion; shows complex interactions in outlier handling.

papers.title: UniCA: Unified Covariate Adaptation for Time Series Foundation Model
papers.contribution: UniCA demonstrates superiority on multiple unimodal and multimodal covariate-aware forecasting benchmarks.

papers.title: Adapt Data to Model: Adaptive Transformation Optimization for Domain-shared Time Series Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Achieves maximum MSE reduction of 68.4% and average decrease of 16.0%, typically optimizing transformation pipelines in under 2 minutes.

papers.title: CauKer: Classification Time Series Foundation Models Can Be Pretrained on Synthetic Data
papers.contribution: CauKer-generated datasets enable sample-efficient pretraining of classification TSFMs and exhibit clear scaling laws from 10K to 10M samples unlike real-world datasets.

papers.title: Channel Adapter for Time Series Foundation Models in Zero-Shot Multivariate Forecasting
Context parroting: A simple but tough-to-beat baseline for foundation models in scientific machine learning
papers.contribution: Context parroting outperforms leading time-series foundation models on chaos, turbulence, oscillators, and ECG at a tiny fraction of computational cost, revealing fundamental limitations in foundation model design.

papers.title: Mantis: Lightweight Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art across four diverse dataset collections via enhanced test-time methodology leveraging intermediate representations, self-ensembling, and embedding fusion.

papers.title: Universal Redundancies in Time Series Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Shows all studied models robust to layer ablation; identifies specific heads responsible for degenerate phenomena like motif parroting and seasonality bias.

papers.title: Zeus: Towards Tuning-Free Foundation Model for Time Series Analysis
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive results across five analysis tasks without tuning; improves performance on out-of-domain benchmarks (+8.06%); code available.
